issues.legal_issue: A revenue authority must refer a stamp-duty case to the High Court when an application raises a substantial question of law, even if the revenue proceedings have concluded.
material_facts: An instrument was presented for registration on the footing that it was a declaration of trust, but it was impounded and sent to the Collector for action concerning deficient stamp duty and penalty.
The Collector imposed duty and penalty, and the controlling revenue authority reduced the amounts on revision.
An application asking the controlling revenue authority to state a case to the High Court was rejected, and the High Court dismissed a petition challenging that refusal.
Whether the instrument was a declaration of trust or a deed of settlement raised a substantial question of law.
issues.conclusion: The controlling revenue authority was required to state the case despite the absence of a pending revenue proceeding. The High Court erred in dismissing the petition; its order was set aside and the authority was directed to state the case.
issues.legal_principle: Section 57(1) of the Indian Stamp Act, 1899, read with sections 56(1) and 59(2), gives a citizen a remedy to obtain a High Court opinion where an application concerning an order imposing stamp duty or penalty raises a substantial question of law, and places a corresponding duty on the controlling revenue authority to state the case. That duty does not depend on whether the revenue case is still pending. The Court relied on Chief Controlling Revenue Authority v. Maharashtra Sugar Mills Ltd., which established the authority’s duty to refer a substantial question of law even after the case had concluded, and on the principle in Alcock Ashdown v. Chief Revenue Authority, Bombay, that a court may grant relief when a public officer fails to perform a statutory duty. The Court also noted analogous provisions governing income-tax references.

predicates.stamp_duty_reference_proceeding: The dispute concerns a revenue authority’s decision imposing stamp duty or a penalty on an instrument.
predicates.reference_application_made: A person applied to the controlling revenue authority to state the case to the High Court.
predicates.substantial_question_of_law: The application raises a substantial question of law.

issues.definition: When a person applies in a stamp-duty reference proceeding and raises a substantial question of law, the controlling revenue authority must state the case to the High Court, whether or not the revenue proceedings remain pending.
